name: abstract-copy
text: X-ray polarimetry adds directional information that imaging, spectroscopy and timing may not fully provide. XPoSat’s POLIX payload records polarization-sensitive azimuthal scattering in the 8–30 keV band and distributes several heterogeneous Level-2 FITS products for each observation. The proposed study aims to represent scientifically meaningful behaviour across these products, screen observations without trusted anomaly labels, and explain unusual scores at both feature and product level. A separate WeightedRoll-based modulation diagnostic is intended to support cautious physical interpretation against blank-sky behaviour. The expected contribution is a traceable researcher-oriented screening framework. Its central limitation is that statistical unusualness and fitted modulation are not equivalent to a calibrated polarization degree, an official sky polarization angle, or an astrophysical discovery.
